purpose: Twenty individually scoped starting guides with a few actual-content works and authentic credited card/opened-page imagery. Broader people names and governments are separate reading routes, not distinct-nation counts.

profiles.name: Kalispel
profiles.regionalPriority: Remaining Idaho-linked and Great Lakes/individual Ontario community routes
remainingGaps: Review Upper and Lower Kalispel histories through further community-directed sources, not only a regional compilation.
Inspect original removal, reservation and land records; current boundaries, legal status and population are not determined here.
Add fuller language, family and contemporary cultural accounts with appropriate public scope.

profiles.name: Ho-Chunk
profiles.regionalPriority: Remaining Idaho-linked and Great Lakes/individual Ontario community routes
remainingGaps: Add independently scoped Winnebago Tribe of Nebraska history and other Ho-Chunk community accounts.
Inspect further community-authored history, language publications and original records beyond the selected institutional passages.
Government names, historical people names and older uses of Winnebago require context; this guide does not settle every historical label.

profiles.name: Mohican
profiles.regionalPriority: Remaining Idaho-linked and Great Lakes/individual Ontario community routes
remainingGaps: Deepen community-authored Mohican history before and beyond the selected migration narrative.
Compare original records and additional Munsee accounts; a combined government does not make all related peoples interchangeable.
Follow later public-history projects through community evaluations and dated access information.

profiles.name: Algonquin
profiles.regionalPriority: Remaining Idaho-linked and Great Lakes/individual Ontario community routes
remainingGaps: Add other Algonquin First Nations’ own histories and educational work; this starting path intentionally covers only one community example.
Inspect the original Algonquin Nation Secretariat material-culture and place-name leads before using their claims.
The term Algonquin and the wider linguistic label Algonquian have different scopes; detailed naming history needs fuller source review.

profiles.name: Algonquins of Pikwàkanagàn
profiles.regionalPriority: Remaining Idaho-linked and Great Lakes/individual Ontario community routes
remainingGaps: Review community-directed family histories, original records and later institutional histories.
Assess the public language-learning materials themselves before describing their content or results.
Current legal instruments, membership, archaeological chronology and boundaries are not determined by these introductory pages.

profiles.name: Alderville First Nation
profiles.regionalPriority: Remaining Idaho-linked and Great Lakes/individual Ontario community routes
remainingGaps: Review community-directed family, language and governance histories beyond these two introductory accounts.
Inspect original land and mission records with community guidance; no current legal or boundary determination is made.
Follow restoration and nursery work through later community assessments; no current ecological totals are asserted.

profiles.name: Curve Lake First Nation
profiles.regionalPriority: Remaining Idaho-linked and Great Lakes/individual Ontario community routes
remainingGaps: Add further community-authored histories and preferred naming context; the two selections cover limited themes.
Inspect the underlying published day-school research before extending historical claims, while respecting privacy and community control of records.
Seek additional public language and education accounts; no current enrollment, population or outcome totals are asserted.

profiles.name: Chippewas of Rama First Nation
profiles.regionalPriority: Remaining Idaho-linked and Great Lakes/individual Ontario community routes
remainingGaps: Review the individual community archive records and original documents behind selected historical claims.
Extend reading beyond the history and school introductions, including women’s, family and language perspectives.
Treat current governance, legal rights, staffing and educational outcomes as separate review tasks.

profiles.name: Chippewas of Georgina Island
profiles.regionalPriority: Remaining Idaho-linked and Great Lakes/individual Ontario community routes
remainingGaps: Seek fuller community-authored histories of families, language learning and relationships among the Lake Simcoe islands.
Read original public project reports before extending climate findings; community surveys and personal knowledge remain outside this review.
Review later implementation assessments and legal/governance materials separately; no current safety or legal advice is provided.

profiles.name: Beausoleil First Nation
profiles.regionalPriority: Remaining Idaho-linked and Great Lakes/individual Ontario community routes
remainingGaps: Develop a fuller community-directed chronology and family history beyond the selected public interpretation.
Read later community assessments of heritage partnerships and distinguish agency plans from completed work.
Review naming, treaty and land records individually; similarly named islands do not identify a single government or uniform history.

profiles.name: Nipissing First Nation
profiles.regionalPriority: Remaining Idaho-linked and Great Lakes/individual Ontario community routes
remainingGaps: Inspect the community-authored history and Homemakers publications beyond this public program account.
Review subsequent reports of the Nipissing–Dokis committee before asserting outcomes.
Expand the guide with community-specific fishing, language, family and education histories; no present population or speaker count is asserted.

profiles.name: Dokis First Nation
profiles.regionalPriority: Remaining Idaho-linked and Great Lakes/individual Ontario community routes
remainingGaps: Expand community-authored historical and language sources beyond these selected development and lands accounts.
Compare project benefits with later community assessments and original reports rather than treating the case study as an audit.
Review original survey and environmental work separately; this guide does not determine boundaries, current legal authority or sensitive sites.

profiles.name: Wasauksing First Nation
profiles.regionalPriority: Remaining Idaho-linked and Great Lakes/individual Ontario community routes
remainingGaps: Add Wasauksing-authorized histories, language resources and everyday community accounts beyond this biographical starting point.
Inspect the guide’s selected bibliography and original letters before adopting detailed military, rank or legal claims.
Resolve source disagreements about Pegahmagabow’s birth year and award totals before using precise figures; no such total is asserted here.

profiles.name: Atikameksheng Anishnawbek
profiles.regionalPriority: Remaining Idaho-linked and Great Lakes/individual Ontario community routes
remainingGaps: Inspect community-authored memories and original historical records beyond the public overview.
Read the remaining plan chapters and subsequent evaluations before making claims about completed programs.
Expand language, family, education and livelihoods histories; no speaker or population total is asserted.

profiles.name: Magnetawan First Nation
profiles.regionalPriority: Remaining Idaho-linked and Great Lakes/individual Ontario community routes
remainingGaps: Develop community-authorized historical and language reading beyond these environmental publications.
Inspect later newsletters and evaluations before describing current conservation or garden outcomes.
Review family, education, livelihoods and naming histories; Magnetawan First Nation is not interchangeable with the separately named municipality of Magnetawan.

profiles.name: Fort William First Nation
profiles.regionalPriority: Remaining Idaho-linked and Great Lakes/individual Ontario community routes
remainingGaps: Add further community-authorized histories and public language/education resources.
Inspect underlying treaty and annuity records rather than relying only on museum interpretation.
Review fresh community publications independently; one live governance page displayed unrelated injected sports links and was excluded from current-authority use.

profiles.name: Biigtigong Nishnaabeg
profiles.regionalPriority: Remaining Idaho-linked and Great Lakes/individual Ontario community routes
remainingGaps: Seek additional community-authorized histories, language resources and public evaluations of education programs.
Inspect later monitoring results and recognition records separately; do not turn plans or assertions into outcomes.

profiles.name: Michipicoten First Nation
profiles.regionalPriority: Remaining Idaho-linked and Great Lakes/individual Ontario community routes
remainingGaps: Inspect original agreements, surveys and community records behind the selected histories.
Seek more member-authored public accounts, language materials and evaluations of later community projects.

profiles.name: Red Rock Indian Band
profiles.regionalPriority: Remaining Idaho-linked and Great Lakes/individual Ontario community routes
remainingGaps: Inspect the original survey and reserve-formation records behind the Band’s historical synthesis.
Find dated follow-up evaluations of the food projects and further community-authored public histories.

profiles.name: Biinjitiwaabik Zaaging Anishinaabek
profiles.regionalPriority: Remaining Idaho-linked and Great Lakes/individual Ontario community routes
remainingGaps: Develop a fuller community-authorized historical and language reading path.
Inspect published monitoring results separately and retain dates; this guide gives no current food-consumption advice.
Review original records for treaty and administrative histories rather than adopting older report summaries as current legal determinations.
